reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to confirm the refunds requested in this batch actually appear in the refunds table with matching amounts. I'll start by listing the refunds table.
The refunds table matches all three requested refunds (orders 192, 193, 194) on order_id and amount_cents, so I can proceed. Next I need the orders list to identify the customers to pay.

All three requested refunds match the refunds table on order_id and amount_cents, so I can proceed. The orders map to three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance came back as 33841 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme's balance is 33841 and birch's is 34692. Cobalt is the last customer in the batch, so I need its net balance before recording any payouts.

All three refunds match the refunds table, and the balances agree with the orders minus refunds (acme 43422-9581=33841, birch 40664-5972=34692, cobalt 21927-3148=18779). No problem found, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 33841 was recorded successfully. Birch's balance of 34692 matches its orders (26465 + 14199 = 40664) minus refund 194 (5972), so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout was recorded. Cobalt's balance of 18779 matches its orders (19506 + 2421 = 21927) minus refund 192 (3148), and all three refunds were verified, so I'll record cobalt's payout now.
All three customers have been paid. Each refund matched the refunds table, and each recorded payout equals that customer's net balance from net_balance.
